paper_id: Li and Liu - 2007 - Rendered path range-free localization in anisotropic sensor networks with holes
title: Rendered Path: Range-Free Localization in Anisotropic Sensor Networks with Holes
motivation: Range-based schemes need expensive hardware; range-free schemes need many uniformly-deployed seeds and fail when holes exist in practical deployments
problem_framing: How to estimate Euclidean distance between nodes purely from hop-count in anisotropic networks where holes break hop-to-distance proportionality
key_insight: Hole boundaries can be colored and rendered on shortest paths; comparing original path with augmented virtual-hole path recovers angle and distance information
method_signature: REP renders shortest paths with colored boundary nodes, constructs virtual holes around focal nodes, and calculates distance from two rendered paths
evaluation_criteria: Distance estimation error (%) and localization error (meters) across varying node density and network geometry complexity
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Approach involves routes exponentially increasing with number of holes in worst case, incurring significant overhead
evidence_for_taste: REP is the only range-free protocol
DV-hop is the only approach which employs a constant number of seeds
This approach involves routes exponentially increasing
thinking_moves: 把距离估计问题从几何感知重新frame为路径通信问题
通过人为制造干扰(虚拟孔)来探测原始几何结构
用两条渲染路径的差异反推角度信息
承认最坏情况下复杂度爆炸，但用技巧性解法缓解
